profile.name: Hana Girma
profile.title: Product Engineer
profile.bio: I design and build calm, fast web products for people who are busy doing their real job: clinic staff, school administrators and small-shop owners across East Africa.
profile.currently_learning: Rust for WebAssembly, and Amharic typography

about.heading: About me
about.title: I build software that respects people's time
about.description: I grew up translating forms for my grandmother at the kebele office, which is probably where my obsession with clear interfaces started. Today I work across the stack — product discovery, interface design, React front ends and Django back ends — and I'm happiest when a feature ships and nobody needs a manual to use it.
about.description_2: Over six years I've shipped booking systems for clinics, a payments dashboard used by 1,200 merchants, and an offline-first attendance app for rural schools. I care about performance on cheap Android phones, bilingual (Amharic/English) interfaces, and leaving codebases better documented than I found them.
about.interests:
Long-distance running around Entoto
Ethiopian jazz records (Mulatu Astatke on repeat)
Teaching a weekend coding class for girls
Hand-lettering Ge'ez script
Testing every macchiato in Piassa

principles.title: Ship small, ship often
principles.description: A working slice in users' hands beats a perfect plan. I aim for something demoable every week.

principles.title: Design for the slowest phone
principles.description: If it's fast on a three-year-old Android on 3G, it's fast everywhere.

principles.title: Write it down
principles.description: Decisions, trade-offs and how-tos live in the repo, so the team doesn't depend on my memory.

principles.title: Measure the outcome
principles.description: Every feature starts with the number it should move, and I check it after launch.

projects.title: Tena Booking
projects.summary: Appointment booking for private clinics, rebuilt around how reception staff actually work.
projects.overview: Tena Booking is the scheduling core of Tena Health's clinic suite. Patients book by phone, Telegram or the web; reception staff manage a shared calendar across doctors, rooms and equipment.
projects.problem: Clinics were losing a fifth of bookings to double-booked rooms and no-shows. The old flow took seven screens, worked badly on the cheap tablets at reception desks, and had no Amharic interface.
projects.results: Booking time at the desk dropped from about two minutes to under forty seconds, and SMS reminders cut no-shows by almost a third within the first quarter.

features.title: Three-step booking
features.description: Pick a service, pick a time, confirm. Doctor and room are assigned automatically.

features.title: Resource-aware calendar
features.description: Doctors, rooms and equipment are booked together, so double-booking is impossible.

features.title: Bilingual reminders
features.description: SMS and Telegram reminders in Amharic or English, 24 hours and 2 hours before.

features.title: Works on reception tablets
features.description: Lightweight UI that stays fast on low-end Android tablets.

architecture.description: A Django API with PostgreSQL exclusion constraints guaranteeing no overlapping bookings per resource. Reminders run as Redis-backed background jobs. The React front end is code-split per role (reception, doctor, admin).

challenges.problem: Double bookings when two receptionists booked the same slot at once.
challenges.solution: Moved the rule into the database with an exclusion constraint on (resource, time range), and showed a friendly conflict message with the next free slots.

challenges.problem: Staff didn't trust the new calendar.
challenges.solution: Ran the old and new systems side by side for two weeks with a daily diff report, until the numbers matched.

lessons.title: Sit at the reception desk
lessons.description: Two days watching receptionists taught us more than a month of interviews.

projects.title: Birr Pay Merchant Dashboard
projects.summary: Payouts, refunds and reconciliation for 1,200 merchants, fast on a mid-range phone.
projects.overview: The merchant-facing dashboard for Birr Pay: daily payouts, refunds, disputes and downloadable statements.
projects.problem: Merchants called support to ask "where is my money?" because the old dashboard took over four seconds to load and showed raw transaction codes.
projects.results: Support calls about payouts fell by half, and the dashboard became the most-used page in the product.

features.title: Plain-language payouts
features.description: Every payout shows when, how much and why — no transaction codes.

features.title: Nightly reconciliation
features.description: Bank statements are matched to transactions automatically, with mismatches flagged for finance.

challenges.problem: Statements from three banks used three different formats.
challenges.solution: Wrote a small parser per bank behind one interface, with fixture files from real (anonymised) statements as tests.

projects.title: Kuteba — Offline-first School Attendance for Rural Ethiopia
projects.summary: Attendance and reporting app that works for weeks without a connection and syncs when it can.
projects.overview: Teachers take attendance on a shared Android phone; data syncs to the regional education office whenever there's signal.
projects.problem: Paper registers took weeks to reach the woreda office, so dropouts were noticed months too late.
projects.results: Piloted in 18 schools; the office now sees attendance within a day and follows up on absences in the same week.

features.title: Weeks offline
features.description: Everything is stored locally and synced with conflict-free merge when back online.

features.title: Ge'ez calendar
features.description: Dates are shown in the Ethiopian calendar, as teachers expect.
